title: Non-blocking follow-ups from PR #113 review (scripts-validate-tasks)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #113 (scripts-validate-tasks), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: Fix scripts/validate_tasks.py's dead 'id field does not match its filename' check: check_task_shape(task_id, data) is always called with task_id already derived as data["id"] when data has a non-empty id (see collect_task_files/run: `task_id = data["id"] if is_nonempty_str(data.get("id")) else path.stem`), so the internal comparison `data["id"] != task_id` inside check_task_shape can never be true -- the check is unreachable dead code. Verified by hand: adding a task file docs/tasks/scratch-filename-mismatch.json with `"id": "totally-different-id"` produced zero violation for this specific rule (only the unrelated 'missing index.json entry' violation fired). Fix by passing the filename-derived id (path.stem) separately into check_task_shape so it can genuinely compare against the file's own `id` field, independent of which value it uses elsewhere as the task's canonical id.

Add a persisted, committed regression test for scripts/validate_tasks.py itself (e.g. a small stdlib-only test script or a pytest module) exercising each violation type on synthetic fixture data, plus the real-board clean-pass case. The task-worker's smoke test (a synthetic negative-case run covering every violation type, per the task's checklist item 4) was apparently run ad hoc and not committed, so there's currently no automated way to re-verify the validator's own correctness on a future change to it -- and, notably, a committed test suite would have caught both the dead id-vs-filename check and the TypeError-on-non-scalar-field crash bug (both fixed as blocking findings on this same PR) if those specific cases had been included.

scripts/validate_tasks.py's `tasks_by_id[task_id] = (data, path)` (in `run()`) silently overwrites an earlier entry when two task files share the same `id` (e.g. a stale copy left behind after an incomplete `git mv` to docs/tasks/done/). The duplicate is flagged once as "duplicate id ... found elsewhere on the board", but every subsequent cross-check (index.json state/path mirror, depends_on resolution) then only ever runs against whichever file was processed last -- a genuine, independent drift on the earlier/stale duplicate is never separately checked beyond that one generic line. Consider keying by (task_id, path) for the cross-check loops, or at least noting in the duplicate-id violation message that only one of the copies was cross-checked.

Non-blocking (round 2, PR #113): `scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py` carries a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang but isn't chmod +x (unlike `scripts/validate_tasks.py`, which is), so a bare `ruff check scripts/` (no top-level pyproject.toml/ruff.toml, so ruff falls back to its own default rule set rather than backend's configured `select`) reports one `EXE001` finding on it. Not part of the enforced lint gate (no top-level ruff config exists for `scripts/`, same precedent as `backend/scripts/`), and the file's own docstring already documents running it via `python3 scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py`, not direct execution, so this is cosmetic. Fix by either `chmod +x` on the file or dropping the shebang line since it isn't meant to be run directly.

Non-blocking (round 2, PR #113): the four `isinstance(value, str) and value not in <VALID_SET>` guards added to fix the PR #113 round-1 TypeError crash (test.verdict, review.verdict, test.gap_analysis[].severity, index.json per-task state) are near-identical inline blocks. task-worker's own `decisions` entry on the parent task already considered and rejected a shared `expect_str_in(value, valid_set, field_name)` helper for round 2 to keep that diff minimal; worth revisiting as a small follow-up simplification since the duplication is now a permanent fixture of the file, not just a two-line fix.

Non-blocking (round 2, PR #113, surfaced by an independent code-review pass after the accept was posted): `run()`'s `index_by_id[task_id] = entry` (around line 307) has the exact same overwrite-on-duplicate bug that `tasks_by_id` had before this PR fixed it on the task-file side -- when `docs/tasks/index.json` itself contains two entries sharing the same `id`, only the last-processed entry survives in `index_by_id`, so the state/path mirror cross-check later in `run()` only ever compares the real task file against that last entry. Reproduced directly: a scratch `index.json` with two `id: "dupidx"` entries (one `state: "planned"`, one `state: "implementing"`, task file itself `state: "implementing"`) produces only the single `duplicate id 'dupidx' in tasks list` violation -- the first entry's genuine drift (`planned` vs. the file's real `implementing`) is never independently reported, unlike the equivalent scenario on the task-file side (which the `tasks_by_id` fix in this same PR already handles by keying to a list of entries). Judged non-blocking rather than blocking, consistent with the precedent set by the original (pre-fix) `tasks_by_id` finding in round 1, which was also filed non-blocking: a duplicate id in `index.json` already surfaces its own violation, prompting a human/agent to consolidate the entries directly, which incidentally resolves the missed mirror-check too, and it only actually hides a real defect when the *earlier* duplicate (not the one that happens to be processed last) is the one with the stale value. Fix by keying `index_by_id` to a list of entries (mirroring the `tasks_by_id` fix already in this file) and iterating all of them in the mirror cross-check loop.

decisions.decision: All three non-blocking checklist items here were fixed as part of PR #113's needs_work revision (scripts-validate-tasks), not deferred to a separate task-worker pass on this task id: (1) check_task_shape now takes filename_stem as its own parameter and compares data['id'] against that instead of against the already-id-derived task_id; (2) tasks_by_id in run() now maps id -> list of (data, path) and both cross-check loops (depends_on resolution, index.json mirror) iterate every entry in that list, so a duplicate id's earlier copy is no longer dropped from cross-checking; (3) a persisted stdlib-only regression suite now lives at scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py (23 tests, run via `python3 scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py`), covering every violation category including these two fixes and a real-board clean-pass smoke test.
decisions.rationale: PR #113's needs_work review required fixing two blocking findings in the exact same function (check_task_shape) and file (scripts/validate_tasks.py) these three non-blocking findings also touch, and the review's own notes on finding #2 (the missing regression suite) pointed out that a committed test suite would likely have caught the two blocking bugs -- so writing that suite now, alongside the blocking fixes and while the failure modes are fresh, was more valuable than leaving all three for a later, separate task-worker dispatch against already-drifted code. This task (scripts-validate-tasks-followups) is left in state 'planned' rather than being marked 'done' here: fixing the code is within task-worker's authority for the parent task's own PR, but formally closing a different tracked task's checklist (including any QA/review pass CLAUDE.md's pipeline expects before a state change to 'done') belongs to that task's own dispatch, not a side effect of fixing the parent task on the parent's branch/PR.
decisions.alternatives_considered: Considered leaving these three items for a dedicated future task-worker run against this task id instead, per the parent task's own instruction that addressing them now was 'not strictly required'; rejected in favor of fixing them immediately since all three are small, isolated to code already being edited for the blocking fixes, and (per the rationale above) directly reduce the risk of re-shipping the same class of bug the blocking findings surfaced.

decisions.decision: Fixed the remaining three round-2 items on this task's own dispatch: (1) index_by_id in validate_tasks.py's run() is now keyed id -> list of entries (mirroring the existing tasks_by_id fix), and the state/path mirror cross-check loop iterates every index.json row sharing an id instead of just one, so an earlier duplicate row's own drift is no longer silently skipped when a later duplicate happens to be non-drifted; (2) dropped the `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang from scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py rather than chmod +x'ing it, since the file's own docstring already documents running it via `python3 scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py`, not direct execution -- a shebang implies direct-execution intent that doesn't match how the file is actually meant to be run; (3) added a shared `is_invalid_str_choice(value, valid_values)` helper used by all four 'must be one of these string values' checks (test.verdict, review.verdict, gap_analysis[].severity, index.json entry state), factoring out only the isinstance-and-membership condition (the part that caused the original TypeError crash bug) while leaving each call site's own violation message wording untouched, so no existing test assertions needed to change.
decisions.rationale: For (1): this is the exact defect the checklist item describes, reproduced and fixed the same way as the task-file-side tasks_by_id bug in the parent PR -- same shape, same fix. For (2): CLAUDE.md's testing standard and this file's own docstring treat it as an importable/subprocess-invoked test module, not a standalone script, so a shebang without the executable bit was dead weight rather than a real omission; dropping it (vs. chmod +x) keeps the file's permission bits matching its actual invocation pattern and avoids adding an executable bit to a file nothing execs directly. For (3): the checklist item explicitly left this to follow-up judgment; a helper that unifies only the condition (not the message) is close to zero-risk -- it changes no observable violation text, so every existing test assertion still passes unmodified -- while still removing the actual duplicated logic (the isinstance+membership check) that was the root cause of the round-1 TypeError crash this file's own regression tests guard against.
decisions.alternatives_considered: For (2), considered chmod +x instead (the other option the checklist text offered); rejected because nothing in the codebase invokes this file as `./scripts/tests/test_validate_tasks.py` and adding an executable bit to a test module not meant for direct execution would be the more surprising choice, not the more conservative one. For (3), considered a fuller helper that also unifies the message text (e.g. `expect_str_in(value, valid_set, field_name) -> str | None` returning a formatted message); rejected because the four messages differ in structure enough (index.json's omits the 'must be one of' phrasing and valid-values echo that the other three include) that unifying them would have required either changing an existing, test-asserted message string or keeping an awkward per-call-site override parameter -- more churn for a purely cosmetic message-format alignment than the actual duplication (the condition) warranted. Also considered leaving all three deferred per the checklist's own 'read the text for what was deferred and use your judgment' framing; rejected because none of the three carried real risk or ambiguity once traced through, and leaving them open would just mean a future task-worker re-reading the same context again.
